description: Single-panel "banana diagram" whose y-axis is labelled "Total Elongation (%)" (0–100, ticks every 20) and x-axis "Ultimate tensile strength (MPa)" (0–1200, ticks every 200). No individual data points are plotted; the property ranges are drawn as filled, elongated ellipses. A rectangular legend box at top left is headed "Density Reduction" and lists three colour-coded ranges: "Ferritic: 7.5-12.7%" in red text, "Fe-Mn-Al-C: 10-20%" in blue text, and "Intermetallics: > 25%" in purple text. Five labelled ellipses, each with an arrow/leader to its text, are present: a red ellipse for "Fe-Al Ferritic steels" at the lowest strength (between the 400 and 600 MPa gridlines, elongation roughly 10–30%); a blue ellipse for "Fe-Mn-Al-C Duplex steels (α + γ)" between about 600 and 800 MPa at 40–60% elongation; a larger blue ellipse for "Fe-Mn-Al-C Triplex steels (γ + α + κ)" at roughly 800–1050 MPa and 45–75% elongation; a blue ellipse for "Fe-Mn-Al-C PH steels (α + κ)" near 800–950 MPa at only 10–20% elongation; and a purple ellipse for "Fe-Al Intermetallics" at the highest strength with low elongation. The plot demonstrates that austenite-bearing duplex and triplex steels reach higher strength–elongation combinations than ferritic or intermetallic steels while also showing larger density reductions.

observations.observation: The plot axes are labelled 'Ultimate tensile strength (MPa)' on the x-axis (0 to 1200, ticks every 200) and 'Total Elongation (%)' on the y-axis (0 to 100, ticks every 20).

A legend box in the upper left titled 'Density Reduction' gives three colour-coded ranges: 'Ferritic: 7.5-12.7%' (red text), 'Fe-Mn-Al-C: 10-20%' (blue text) and 'Intermetallics: > 25%' (purple text).
No individual data points or fitted curves are printed; the property ranges are represented only as five filled ellipse envelopes.
The red ellipse is labelled 'Fe-Al Ferritic steels' and occupies the lowest-strength region, lying between the 400 and 600 MPa gridlines at low-to-intermediate elongation.
The blue ellipse labelled 'Fe-Mn-Al-C Duplex steels (α + γ)' lies between roughly the 600 and 800 MPa gridlines at about 40–60% total elongation.
The largest blue ellipse, labelled 'Fe-Mn-Al-C Triplex steels (γ + α + κ)', extends from about 800 to 1050 MPa with the highest elongation range of the high-strength group (about 45–75%).
A blue ellipse labelled 'Fe-Mn-Al-C PH steels (α + κ)' lies at high strength (approximately 800–950 MPa) but at low elongation (about 10–20%), i.e. to the right of the duplex band but much lower.

The purple ellipse labelled 'Fe-Al Intermetallics' sits at the highest ultimate tensile strength (near/beyond 1000 MPa) with low total elongation, and corresponds to the '> 25%' density reduction legend entry.
The caption titles the figure 'Strength-elongation plot of some low-density steels' and states that density reductions in these steels are also indicated.
The citing text calls this plot the 'banana diagram' and attributes it to reference 20.
According to the citing text, steels containing austenite (duplex and triplex steels) are superior in strength–ductility balance as well as in density reduction compared with ferritic steels.

The citing text attributes that superiority to two factors: different strength- and ductility-enhancing mechanisms operating in the austenite-containing steels, and their higher alloying content (Al and Mn).
The three density-reduction classes in the legend map onto the coloured envelopes: red = ferritic (7.5–12.7%), blue = Fe-Mn-Al-C (10–20%), purple = intermetallics (> 25%).

subfigures.description: One strength–elongation ('banana') chart: y = Total Elongation (%) 0–100, x = Ultimate tensile strength (MPa) 0–1200, with five colour-coded ellipse envelopes labelled Fe-Al Ferritic steels (red), Fe-Mn-Al-C Duplex steels (α + γ), Fe-Mn-Al-C Triplex steels (γ + α + κ), Fe-Mn-Al-C PH steels (α + κ) (blue) and Fe-Al Intermetallics (purple), plus an inset 'Density Reduction' legend listing Ferritic 7.5-12.7%, Fe-Mn-Al-C 10-20%, Intermetallics > 25%.
